headline: Good news on Malaysia labor market by July: Expatriates' Welfare Minister announces
summary: The Expatriates' Welfare Minister has announced that positive developments concerning the Malaysian labor market are expected to be revealed by July. This update brings hope for Bangladeshi job seekers.
details: The Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Minister recently stated that significant positive news regarding the Malaysian labor market is anticipated by July. This announcement offers a ray of hope for thousands of Bangladeshi workers seeking overseas employment.

The minister's statement suggests ongoing discussions and negotiations between Bangladesh and Malaysia to streamline the process for Bangladeshi migrant workers. This development is crucial for addressing the challenges faced by expatriates.

The government has been actively working to ensure a fair and transparent recruitment process, aiming to protect the rights and welfare of Bangladeshi workers abroad. Further details are expected to be disclosed once agreements are finalized.
caption:
Good news is on the horizon for Bangladeshi workers eyeing Malaysia! The Expatriates' Welfare Minister expects positive developments by July.

The Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Minister recently stated that significant positive news regarding the Malaysian labor market is anticipated by July. This announcement offers a ray of hope for thousands of Bangladeshi workers seeking overseas employment.

The minister's statement suggests ongoing discussions and negotiations between Bangladesh and Malaysia to streamline the process for Bangladeshi migrant workers. This development is crucial for addressing the challenges faced by expatriates.

The government has been actively working to ensure a fair and transparent recruitment process, aiming to protect the rights and welfare of Bangladeshi workers abroad. Further details are expected to be disclosed once agreements are finalized.

headline_marked: [[Switzerland tops World Cup Group B]] with 2-1 win over Canada; co-hosts also make historic knockout debut
headline: Switzerland tops World Cup Group B with 2-1 win over Canada; co-hosts also make historic knockout debut
summary: Switzerland secured first place in Group B with seven points after a 2-1 victory against Canada. Despite the loss, Canada advanced to the last 32 for the first time in their history.
details: Ruben Vargas and Johan Manzambi fired Switzerland to top spot in World Cup Group B on Wednesday with a 2-1 win over co-hosts Canada. The victory secured a potentially kinder draw for the Swiss in the knockout stages.
Despite the loss, Canada also ensured a historic spot in the knockout rounds, marking their first-ever qualification for the last 32. They finished three points behind Switzerland in the group.

Prior to this 2026 edition, the North Americans had never won a match at a finals. Canada will now play the runner-up from Group A on Sunday in Los Angeles, while Switzerland returns to Vancouver to meet one of the best third-placed sides next week.
The match sparked into life seconds after the interval, with Vargas giving Switzerland the lead. Manzambi then doubled the score in the 57th minute, netting his third goal of the tournament.
Promise David pulled a goal back for Canada in the final 15 minutes, setting up a grandstand finish. However, Switzerland held on to claim the top spot in the group.
Before kick-off, Canada midfielder Ismael Kone, who suffered a leg break in a previous match, entered the pitch in a wheelchair and received a standing ovation from spectators at BC Place Vancouver.
caption:
Switzerland clinched top spot in World Cup Group B with a 2-1 win over co-hosts Canada. This marks Canada's historic first-ever qualification for the knockout rounds.

Ruben Vargas and Johan Manzambi fired Switzerland to top spot in World Cup Group B on Wednesday with a 2-1 win over co-hosts Canada. The victory secured a potentially kinder draw for the Swiss in the knockout stages.

Despite the loss, Canada also ensured a historic spot in the knockout rounds, marking their first-ever qualification for the last 32. They finished three points behind Switzerland in the group.

Prior to this 2026 edition, the North Americans had never won a match at a finals. Canada will now play the runner-up from Group A on Sunday in Los Angeles, while Switzerland returns to Vancouver to meet one of the best third-placed sides next week.

The match sparked into life seconds after the interval, with Vargas giving Switzerland the lead. Manzambi then doubled the score in the 57th minute, netting his third goal of the tournament.

Promise David pulled a goal back for Canada in the final 15 minutes, setting up a grandstand finish. However, Switzerland held on to claim the top spot in the group.

Before kick-off, Canada midfielder Ismael Kone, who suffered a leg break in a previous match, entered the pitch in a wheelchair and received a standing ovation from spectators at BC Place Vancouver.
